public_rationale: The $125 billion capex minimum matches Meta's guidance. The revenue assertion is harder to settle. Meta reported growth in AI glasses sales before the post, which is material counterevidence to a broad reading. But those sales do not isolate the contribution of AI, and the claim supplies no accounting or attribution measure. A firm verdict would depend on a definition the speaker did not provide.
limitations: Capex guidance is not realized expenditure or exclusively AI expenditure.
Management's sales-growth statement is not a quantified measure of incremental revenue caused by AI.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Meta has not shown real revenue growth from AI despite planning at least $125B of 2026 capex.

statement.excerpt: Sidenote: In all honesty, I have no idea how Meta makes this make sense, as it plans to invest at least $125 billion in capex in 2026 and has, to this point, not shown any actual, real growth in its revenue from AI, and no, those increases in conversion don’t mean actual revenue.

from_speaker: at least $125 billion in capex in 2026
not shown any actual, real growth in its revenue from AI
those increases in conversion don’t mean actual revenue
our_interpretation: The capex statement concerns guidance announced by publication, not expenditure already incurred.
The revenue statement concerns demonstrated growth attributable to AI. Conversion improvements alone do not establish the amount of additional revenue.
Use January–March 2026, the latest reported quarter before publication, for the ongoing revenue observation. Examine disclosures available through May 19.
AI product sales are relevant counterevidence, but revenue from hardware containing AI does not by itself isolate revenue caused by AI.
The single metric_scope describes the disputed revenue component; the separate capex guidance has its own evidence scope.
criteria.support_condition: Contemporaneous guidance has a lower bound of at least $125 billion, and sufficiently complete disclosures establish that Meta had demonstrated no revenue growth attributable to AI under a consistent definition.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Contemporaneous guidance falls below the stated minimum, or Meta had demonstrated positive revenue growth attributable to AI, beyond conversion or engagement improvements alone.
